drafted_from: tools/package-store-reviews (data/generic-record-contracts.json, do-work/validate-action-input.ts and the projection public-reader)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:keep-store-reviews with store {\"where\": \"postgresql database example_me on my own computer\", \"language\": \"SQL (PostgreSQL)\", \"credential_name\": \"example-me-postgres-connection\"} and write a statement by u1 on app-a: score 5, title \"Great\", body \"Works\", visibility public." It keeps the review in your own database and lists the public reviews.
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: the reviews are kept in the person's own store, in whatever form that store keeps them, and store says where and in which language.
instructions: 1. Keep the store's login in your vault under a name you choose, and say where the reviews are kept and how the store is spoken to.
2. Say "Run workflow:keep-store-reviews" with store and the write: a statement, response, vote or concern.
3. The first run makes the review rows once and proves the writes on the example reviews: every expected outcome and answer must match, or the run stops and says which.
4. Every later run keeps the write, refuses a rating outside 1 to 5 or an unknown visibility, and lists the public reviews with their counts.

worked_examples.title: A public review of an app
worked_examples.ask: Review app-a: five stars, Great, it works.

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The look step found no review of app-a from u1; the prove step matched every expected outcome and answer.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "kept" and the public review "r1" with score 5 and title "Great".

worked_examples.title: A rating above five is refused

store.where: postgresql database example_me on my own computer

worked_examples.given: The rating 9 is outside the range from 1 to 5.
worked_examples.hands_back: outcome "refused" with the reason "rating must be from 1 to 5"; nothing is kept.
